:::{#exm-surprisal-chain-rule-reversed-noisy-copy}
#### Chain rule for surprisal with the conditioning reversed, for a noisy copy
<!-- no-figure: the example reports a handful of numbers, with nothing to plot -->

For the pair of values in @exm-joint-conditional-surprisal,
$\P(X=0, Y=1) = 0.1$, $\P(Y=1) = 0.5$ and $\P(X=0 \mid Y=1) = 0.2$.
The chunk computes the three [surprisals](#def-surprisal) in [bits](#def-bit).

```{r}
#| code-fold: show
s_xy <- -log2(0.1)
s_y <- -log2(0.5)
s_x_given_y <- -log2(0.2)
c(sum = s_x_given_y + s_y, joint = s_xy)
```

The [conditional surprisal](#def-conditional-surprisal) of $x = 0$ given $y = 1$ plus the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) of $y = 1$
is $`r round(s_x_given_y + s_y, 3)`$ bits.
This sum is the [joint surprisal](#def-joint-surprisal) $\surprisalf{0, 1} = `r round(s_xy, 3)`$ bits
(@lem-surprisal-chain-rule-reversed).

:::
